whatIsWebDev.title: What is Web Development?
whatIsWebDev.description: Web development is building applications, services, or sites that run over the web, whether that's consumer-facing websites or backend enterprise systems delivered through web technologies. It can range from creating simple informational pages to developing complex APIs and client-server systems that power entire organizations. At its core, web development is about using the web as the platform for delivering software and connecting people with the tools or information they need.
whatIsWebDev.readMore: What does a web developer (webutvikler) do? Read about the role

frontend.title: Frontend Development
frontend.description: Frontend web development is about creating the part of a website or app that people directly use. It shapes how users see, click, type, and move through the interface. Ultimately, it bridges design and user experience into a functional product.

backend.title: Backend Development
backend.description: Backend web development is about building the logic, infrastructure, and systems that support a digital product. It handles how data is stored, processed, and shared between different parts of the application. Ultimately, it enables the product to function as an interconnected, intelligent system.

approach.title: My Approach
approach.description: For me, great engineering isn't just about code or metrics, it's about trust. When a client hands you a complex problem, they're trusting that you can deliver value. They rely on you not just to write solutions, but to understand their needs, anticipate risks, and communicate with clarity. Engineering, at its best, is a partnership, where every line of code reflects reliability, every decision reflects integrity, and every outcome strengthens that trust.

why.title: Why Your Business Needs Professional Web Development
paragraphs: Your website is often the first place people encounter your brand it's your digital storefront. In just a few seconds, visitors decide whether to stay and explore or click away. That's why design and usability are critical. A skilled web developer can craft a layout that captures attention and keeps users engaged.

One of the biggest benefits of working with a professional web developer is the chance to build a site that truly reflects your business. Unlike cookie-cutter website builders, custom development gives you freedom. Your website can align perfectly with your brand voice, whether you want something bold and creative or simple and minimalist.

support.title: Support and Maintenance
support.description: A website needs regular updates to stay secure and effective. Ongoing support ensures your site runs smoothly and grows with your business.

ux.title: Improved User Experience
ux.description: Easy navigation, fast loading, and clear design keep visitors engaged and more likely to convert into customers.

responsive.title: Responsiveness
responsive.description: A responsive site adapts to any device, giving users a smooth experience on mobile, tablet, or desktop.

hero.title: Who is a Web Developer?
hero.subtitle: A web developer is the person who builds the digital layer of today’s world. They turn ideas into websites, apps, and online tools that people use every day.

what.title: What Does a Web Developer Do?
what.description: A web developer creates websites and applications that run on the internet. Some focus on what you see and use, others focus on what happens in the background—but together, they make the web work.
what.imageAlt: Illustration of frontend (a browser window with interface elements) connected to backend (servers and databases)

frontend.title: Frontend web developer: what the user sees
frontend.description: Frontend developers work on the interface. They make sure everything looks right, loads fast, and reacts when you click or type.

backend.title: Backend web developer: the logic behind the scenes
backend.description: Backend developers work on the hidden logic. They handle data, security, servers, and everything that makes the system run reliably.

skills.title: Skills That Shape a Web Developer
skills.description: A good developer doesn’t just know code—they understand how people use the web and how businesses grow online.

items.title: Problem solving in web development
items.description: Breaking down complex issues and finding working solutions.

items.title: Design awareness for better user experience
items.description: Knowing how design choices affect usability and flow.

items.title: Technical adaptability: frameworks and web standards
items.description: Staying current with frameworks, languages, and web standards.

items.title: Collaboration with designers, clients and developers
items.description: Working with designers, clients, and other developers to bring ideas to life.

items.title: Performance, security and scalability
items.description: Optimizing for speed, security, and scalability.

items.title: User focus in every website
items.description: Always building with the end-user’s experience in mind.

why.title: Why Web Developers Matter
paragraphs: Every brand needs a digital presence. Without a website or app, you’re invisible to most of your audience.
A skilled web developer helps create tools that don’t just exist—they perform. That means better reach, more engagement, and stronger trust.

points.title: First impressions: a website that keeps visitors
points.description: A visitor’s opinion forms in seconds. Good development keeps them engaged.

points.title: A scalable website that grows with your business
points.description: A strong foundation allows your site or app to grow with your business.

points.title: A reliable website with minimal downtime
points.description: Secure, stable, and well-maintained systems prevent downtime and protect your data.

technologies.title: Technologies a Modern Web Developer Uses
technologies.intro: Tools change quickly, but some technologies have become the standard for websites and web applications in Norway. These are the ones I use most in my work as a web developer in Oslo.

items.title: React: reusable components
items.description: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces from small, reusable components. It makes large solutions easier to maintain and develop further.

items.title: Next.js: fast, search-friendly pages
items.description: Next.js builds on React and adds server rendering, static generation, and routing. The result is pages that load fast and that Google can read easily.

items.title: WordPress: a proven publishing tool
items.description: WordPress powers a large share of the world's websites. It is a good fit when editors want to update content themselves and the budget calls for a well-known platform.

items.title: Sanity: headless CMS for structured content
items.description: Sanity separates content from presentation. Editors get a tidy tool, while the developer is free to show the content on a website, an app, or other channels.

items.title: Node.js: JavaScript on the server
items.description: With Node.js, backend logic, APIs, and integrations can be written in the same language as the frontend. That shortens the path from idea to working solution.

become.title: How Do You Become a Web Developer?
become.intro: There is no single path into the profession. Some take a bachelor's degree in computer science or web development, others attend vocational college, take an intensive course, or teach themselves everything. Employers care most about what you can actually show.

steps.title: Learn the foundation: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
steps.description: Everything on the web is built on these three. Understand them well before jumping to frameworks, and the rest becomes much easier.

steps.title: Pick one framework and go deep
steps.description: React is among the most requested skills in web developer job listings. Once you master it, the step to Next.js is short.

steps.title: Build a portfolio of your own projects
steps.description: Real projects say more than a diploma. Build a website for a friend, a local club, or an idea of your own, and publish the code on GitHub.

steps.title: Learn Git and teamwork
steps.description: Version control, code review, and dialogue with designers are as much a part of the job as the coding itself.

steps.title: Apply for junior roles or take small gigs
steps.description: Junior positions, trainee programs, and smaller freelance gigs give valuable experience. The most important thing is to get started and keep learning.

become.outro: I have worked as a web developer since 2004 myself, and I still learn something new every week. The profession rewards curiosity more than anything else.

employment.title: Freelancer, Consultant, or Employee?
employment.intro: Web developers work in different ways. Which model fits best depends on the project, the budget, and how long you need help.

options.title: Freelance web developer: flexible and direct
options.description: A freelance web developer takes on work on their own account and bills by the hour or per project. You get direct contact with the person writing the code, and often lower costs than with a large agency.

options.title: Consultant: broad experience from many projects
options.description: A consultant is employed by a consultancy and hired out to clients. I work as a consultant at OsloWeb AS myself, where I have delivered solutions for everything from municipalities to tech companies. The client gets experience and a company behind it.

options.title: In-house web developer: long-term ownership
options.description: An in-house developer knows the product and the organization in depth. It pays off when you have a digital product that will be developed continuously over several years.

price.title: How Much Does a Web Developer Cost?
price.intro: The price depends on scope, complexity, and who you hire. The figures below are approximate price levels in the Norwegian market, excluding VAT. They are meant as a guideline, not as a quote.

ranges.title: Hourly rate for a web developer
ranges.description: Freelancers are often at the lower end of the range, while agencies and consultancies tend to be higher.

ranges.title: Simple business website
ranges.description: A presentation site with a few subpages, a contact form, and a publishing tool such as WordPress or Sanity.

ranges.title: Custom web solution
ranges.range: typically from approx. NOK 50,000 and up
ranges.description: Online stores, web applications, and integrations with other systems require more planning, development, and testing.

price.note: Also remember ongoing costs for hosting, domain, licenses, and maintenance. Always ask for a written estimate before the project starts, so you know what you are paying for.

choose.title: How to Choose the Right Web Developer
choose.intro: Whether you are looking for a web developer in Oslo or elsewhere in the country, a few simple questions separate the good ones from the rest.

tips.title: Look at previous projects
tips.description: Ask for examples of websites the developer has built. Check whether they load fast and work well on mobile.

tips.title: Ask why, not just what
tips.description: A good web developer explains why a technology suits you, not just which tool they personally like best.

tips.title: Clarify ownership and maintenance
tips.description: Make sure you own the code, the domain, and the content, and that there is a plan for updates after launch.

tips.title: Judge the communication
tips.description: You should understand what is happening in the project. If the developer answers clearly and quickly even before you have signed, that is a good sign.

choose.outro: Being local can also be an advantage. A web developer near you can meet you face to face, knows your market, and is easy to reach when something is urgent.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about web developers

items.question: What does a web developer do?
items.answer: A web developer builds and maintains websites and web-based solutions. The work covers everything from what visitors see in the browser (frontend) to the servers, databases and logic behind it (backend).

items.question: What is the difference between frontend and backend?
items.answer: Frontend is the part of a website users see and interact with, such as layout, buttons and forms. Backend is what happens behind the scenes, such as data storage, login and integrations with other systems.

items.question: How much does it cost to hire a web developer?
items.answer: Hourly rates for a web developer in Norway are often around NOK 800–1,500 excl. VAT, depending on experience and whether you hire a freelancer or an agency. A simple business website typically starts from around NOK 15,000, while larger solutions cost more.

items.question: What skills does a web developer need?
items.answer: The core is HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Many also use frameworks such as React and Next.js, and knowledge of databases, APIs, version control, performance and accessibility is important.

items.question: How do I choose the right web developer?
items.answer: Look at previous projects, ask why a technology suits you, clarify ownership of code and domain, and consider how clearly and quickly the developer communicates.

items.question: Do you work as a web developer in Oslo?
items.answer: Yes, Majid Askarifarsangi is a web developer in Oslo and takes on clients both locally and elsewhere in the country. Get in touch for a no-obligation chat about your project.
